purpose: One table of CLUSTER STATES, driven through BOTH installers, asserting identical
verdicts. client#766 gave the two twins a shared contract (envelope_contract.json)
and that fixed arithmetic agreement. It did not give them shared control flow, and
every divergence since has landed in that gap -- five of them across backend#2220:
1. node ordering (memory,cpu) in bash vs (cpu,memory) in the CLI/ps1
2. [math]::Max(0,..) binding Int32 on ps1, swallowed by a bare catch{} -- machine
sizing was silently DEAD on Windows and no test noticed
3. ps1 coerced unparseable allocatable to 0 and RANKED the node; bash skipped it
4. split provenance lookup: on a failed read ps1 said `installer` (invites a ladder
to overrule a human) while bash said `unknown` (permanently strands an
installer-sized edge). Opposite directions -- neither twin told you the other.
5. bash INFERRED 'too small' from a second `kubectl get nodes -o name` probe, so
unparseable or not-yet-Ready nodes tripped a warning about a machine never
measured; ps1 gated on a parsed node.
The golden vectors in envelope_contract.json cover the arithmetic. What they cannot
cover is behaviour on everything that is NOT a clean measurement -- a node that will
not parse, a values read that fails, a remainder too small to request. Those are
exactly the states the five findings lived in, and each twin decided them alone.
A row added here forces BOTH languages to answer it. That is the property that was
missing.
Regenerate the bash companion after editing: scripts/gen-installer-parity.sh

verdict_fields.size: what the installer writes to RESOURCE_LIMITS / RESOURCE_REQUESTS
verdict_fields.provenance: installer | user | unknown -- who chose that size
verdict_fields.undersized: machine measured, below the training floor, honest remainder written
verdict_fields.unschedulable: machine measured, cannot host even a 1-core/1-GiB run

excluded_from_parity.why: bash gates on its own `has kubectl` helper; the ps1 twin has no equivalent and infers absence from $LASTEXITCODE. Not the same input, so comparing verdicts would compare two different questions. Covered per-twin instead (bats: 'kubectl absent falls back to the static default').

rows.label: viable-single-node
rows.why: the ordinary field case -- an 8c/32Gi box

rows.label: viable-large-node
rows.why: guards the ps1 Int32 overload (divergence 2): 61 GiB in bytes exceeds 2^31

rows.label: heterogeneous-incomparable
rows.why: the anchor tie-break (divergence 1). bash ranked (memory,cpu) and would pick 4c/32Gi; the contract's order is (cpu,memory) so 8c/16Gi wins.

rows.label: node-order-reversed
rows.why: the anchor must not depend on the order the API returned nodes in

rows.label: one-unparseable-one-valid
rows.why: divergence 3. ps1 coerced the bad node to 0 and ranked it, so 16 cores with a memory unit we do not speak took the anchor and dropped the whole machine to the literal.

rows.label: unparseable-cpu-one-valid
rows.why: same as above on the CPU dimension

rows.label: all-nodes-unparseable
rows.why: divergence 5. Nothing was measured, so the literal is right and any claim about machine SIZE is a fabrication -- unschedulable must stay false.

rows.label: below-floor-but-requestable
rows.why: 4 GiB - 3 GiB = 1 GiB, under the 2 GiB floor but still a requestable shape. The honest remainder FITS; the 8 GiB literal would not.

rows.label: too-small-to-request
rows.why: cpu=0 is not a training request, so there is no honest number -- keep the literal and say so. Measured, unlike all-nodes-unparseable.

rows.label: exact-floor
rows.why: 5 GiB - 3 GiB = exactly the 2 GiB floor: viable, not undersized. The off-by-one that decides whether an edge can train.

rows.label: carried-read-fails
rows.why: divergence 4, the fail-unsafe one. Nothing is carried, so the machine is sized and `installer` is the TRUE answer. ps1 used to say installer for a CARRIED size; bash used to say unknown.

rows.label: carried-read-empty
rows.why: the read succeeded but said nothing -- same verdict as a failure, and not `unknown`

rows.label: carried-size-no-marker
rows.why: a pre-#768 release. `unknown` is correct HERE because the read SUCCEEDED and there is genuinely no marker -- and consumers must treat it as a human choice.

rows.label: carried-size-user-marker
rows.why: a deliberate `resources set` must survive re-install without decaying

rows.label: carried-size-installer-marker
rows.why: an installer-written size stays attributable, so a future ladder may re-derive it

rows.label: carried-size-junk-marker
rows.why: anything unrecognised degrades to unknown, never to a guess

rows.label: carried-historic-literal
rows.why: the old cpu=2,memory=8Gi was the ABSENCE of a choice, so it must not be carried -- the machine gets sized instead. A marker beside it does not change that.

rows.label: install-time-override
rows.why: TRACEBLOC_TRAINING_RESOURCES is a human choice, and it wins without probing anything
